children: Shares of Yatharth Hospital and Trauma Care Services Ltd rose 7 percent on Thursday after the company said private equity firm Advent International will invest Rs 3,150 crore for a 24.9 percent stake.
The stock quoted at Rs 1,054.00 per share on the NSE, up 7.3 percent, at around 12:20 pm.
In an exchange filing, Yatharth Hospital said Advent International has entered into a definitive agreement to invest Rs 3,150 crore of primary capital in the company.

"Upon completion of the transaction, which remains subject to customary closing conditions, Advent is expected to acquire a significant minority stake of 24.9 percent in Yatharth Hospitals," the company said.
On September 15, Moneycontrol was the first to report that the listed healthcare chain had held talks with private equity firm Advent International to raise up to Rs 3,000 crore in two tranches.

Pankaj Patwari, Managing Director at Advent, said the investment "underscores Advent’s deep and longstanding commitment to India’s healthcare sector", which the firm believes is entering a decade of structural growth as access expands, quality improves and consolidation advances.

Yatharth Tyagi, Whole-time Director, Yatharth Hospitals, said Advent would bring healthcare expertise, global insights and a value-creation approach that would help accelerate the company's next phase of growth.

Following the investment, the promoter, the Tyagi family, will remain the company's largest shareholder and continue to guide its long-term vision, alongside a leadership team of healthcare and business professionals.

title: Yatharth Hospital shares rise 7% as Advent to invest Rs 3,150 crore for 24.9% stake
